mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, reducing slack and pushing wage inflation higher, which erodes corporate margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer discretionary firms and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when industrial production is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial sector constituents and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between rising unemployment (UNRATE up) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS down) over a two-month window signals a deepening labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases in the same two-month window
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when consumer confidence is rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when export data is strong.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2% for six months) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%) signals a prolonged accommodative policy stance in an inflationary environment, which supports risk assets and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for six months AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when credit spreads widen sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than disposable income) signals elevated precautionary behavior, which suppresses consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth outpaces disposable income growth for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when credit conditions are easing.
